name: input.click
description: Synthesise a mouse click at a virtual-screen coordinate. Affects desktop input state — classified U.

double.description: If true, synthesises a double-click (two press/release pairs within the OS double-click time, see system.info.capabilities.input_settings.double_click_time_ms).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held while clicking. Each modifier is synthesised down before the click and up after.

synthesised.description: True when the input event was accepted by user32's input queue. False indicates the agent detected a UIPI silent-drop (event accepted by the API but never delivered to a higher-IL target window). ERR uipi_blocked is still returned in the latter case; this field also reflects the same signal in the response body.

target_handle.description: Window handle that received the click, resolved via `WindowFromPoint(actual_position)` at synth time. Empty string when the click lands on the desktop or outside any window. Compare against the expected handle to detect target-moved races between window.list/find and the click.

x.description: Actual X the click landed at; differs from input when off-screen requests are clamped to the virtual-screen edge.

y.description: Actual Y the click landed at.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_MOUSE structures. Modifier-down events bracket the click; double batches four mouse events in a single call to stay within `GetDoubleClickTime`.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where `SendInput` is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with INPUT_MOUSE structures. UIPI may silently drop synthesised input directed at higher-IL windows — agent post-checks (e.g. via WindowFromPoint comparison or GetLastInputInfo) and returns ERR uipi_blocked plus `synthesised: false`. When the event reaches user32 the field is true.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; mouse_event on NT 4 and 9x where SendInput is unavailable. No UIPI on classic, so synthesised input crosses process boundaries freely and `synthesised` is true on success.
